source.notes: Official paper page 13 inspected visually, final key lists all four options. Timing and moving-receiver distance are consistent; the wavelength option is convention-sensitive and requires independent scientific adjudication. No silent correction of publisher key.
source.reasoning_observation: Let initial wall distance d=1200 m, train speed u=30 m/s and medium speed v=330 m/s. A pulse reflects and meets the advancing train when vt=2d−ut, giving t=20/3 s and remaining distance1000 m. The printed wavelength choice is v/f=0.60 m, which matches the stationary-source reference, not actual forward wavefront spacing (v−u)/f=6/11 m in the stationary-air moving-source model. Publisher key includes C; preserve disagreement and ask R01 to adjudicate interpretation. No claim that the original is D4.

Derive first echo time and returned frequency, compare with an independent echo frequency450 Hz. Shortest valid route: t=320/340=16/17 s; λ_ahead=300/400=0.75 m. core1a.scientific_construction: In a stationary uniform medium, a subsonic source moving toward a stationary wall emits wavefronts at intervals T_s=1/f_s. Ahead of it the spacing is (v−u)T_s, behind it (v+u)T_s. A pulse emitted at initial wall distance d takes d/v to reach the wall. Its reflected path then meets the moving receiver on the source. If source and receiver remain colocated and approach at speed u, total propagation distance is 2d−ut, so t=2d/(v+u), provided reflection and reception occur before wall contact. A stationary wall reflects the incident frequency in the medium's frame without shifting it. Ahead-of-source frequency at the wall is v f_s/(v−u); for the reflected fronts moving back toward the approaching receiver, encounter rate is (v+u) divided by the forward spacing. Thus f_echo=(v+u)f_s/(v−u). The echo delay is not 2d/v for a moving receiver. These are optional ideal-model extensions; real airflow, motion changes, reflection geometry and source bandwidth require additional constraints. A source at rest has reference wavelength v/f_s; that is not the forward spacing of a moving source.

stages.reconstruct: t=280/360=7/9 s. Remaining distance140−140/9=1120/9 m≈124.44 m. Forward λ=320/300=16/15 m; wall frequency340/(16/15)=318.75 Hz. Reflected encounter frequency360/(16/15)=337.5 Hz. 340/300 is stationary-source reference, not forward spacing; check 340t=140+remaining distance.
